claims.statement: Binance launched in 2017; Binance identifies Changpeng Zhao as co-founder/former CEO, Yi He as co-founder/co-founder-level executive, and Richard Teng as the CEO who succeeded CZ in November 2023.
Binance publicly presents part of its current regulated global structure through ADGM FSRA-regulated Nest entities.
On 2019-05-07 Binance disclosed a security breach involving about 7,000 BTC and said losses would be covered by SAFU.
Binance's current PoR page states user assets are fully backed 1:1 plus reserves, and Binance states the PoR system launched in November 2022.
Binance says SAFU remains its user-emergency fund and that the fund was converted to USDC in 2024.
In November 2023 Binance and CZ resolved U.S. criminal, sanctions and AML matters through a guilty plea and multibillion-dollar settlement package.
BN KZ Technologies Limited is an active AIFC participant; the public company record shows registration date 2021-10-07.
AIFC public materials indicate Binance was registered as an AIFC participant in October 2021 and was undergoing AFSA authorization at that time.
limitations: The supporting AIFC article was surfaced via search excerpt rather than a richer parsed page.

claims.statement: AFSA/AIFC granted Binance in-principle approval on 2022-08-15 to operate a digital asset trading facility and provide custody in the AIFC.
Before full licensing, BN KZ Technologies Limited held two AFSA FinTech Lab licences that became active on 2022-09-29; the second sandbox licence shows futures and options approval on 2024-05-24.
BN KZ Technologies Limited currently appears in the AFSA public register with active licence AFSA-A-LA-2024-0028 from 2024-09-25.

The AFSA public register states that AFSA-A-LA-2024-0028 covers Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility, Dealing in Investments as Principal and Agent, Advising on Investments, Arranging Deals in Investments, Providing Money Services, and Providing Custody.

activities: Operating a Digital Asset Trading Facility

claims.statement: Binance Kazakhstan-facing pages repeat that BN KZ Technologies Limited is authorized by AFSA under licence AFSA-A-LA-2024-0028 to conduct listed activities in or from the AIFC.
AIFC legal materials say activities carried on 'in or from' the AIFC can involve an AIFC participant transacting with parties elsewhere in Kazakhstan or outside Kazakhstan.

AFSA warns that only AFSA-licensed entities may lawfully carry on regulated digital-asset activities in or from the AIFC, and using unlicensed platforms can expose users to legal and consumer-protection risk.
AFSA's 2025 year-end review says Binance Kazakhstan transitioned from the FinTech Lab sandbox to full regulatory status in 2024.
Public Kazakhstan-targeted Binance web surfaces were reachable on the checked date, including the landing page, localized buy/help paths, P2P pages, futures pages, and the Binance app region list.
limitations: Public reachability is not the same as legal authorization or account-level eligibility.

claims.statement: Public registration paths for personal and entity accounts are visible, but no account creation or approval testing was performed.
limitations: This package does not prove successful end-to-end account approval for any Kazakhstan resident.

claims.statement: Binance states that users must complete personal identity verification to unlock trading-related account features, and the flow starts with residence, document issuing country and document type.
Binance KYC and compliance materials show that extra checks can include proof of address, card-gateway checks, and entity/KYB document packages.
For the Freedom Bank KZT rail, Binance requires identity verification and an identification document containing the user's IIN; the withdrawal path also requires an IBAN that matches the IIN details.
Binance publicly documents KZT deposit and withdrawal via Freedom Bank online banking and KZT cash withdrawal to a Kazakhstan-issued Mastercard.
The Mastercard KZT cash-out guide explicitly says the service is only available for customers in Kazakhstan and the card must be issued from Kazakhstan.
Binance's Kazakhstan P2P marketplace is publicly visible with KZT and local payment methods including Home Credit Kazakhstan, Halyk Bank and Freedom Bank.
AFSA's public FAQ says regulated P2P trading is permitted only on licensed AIFC crypto exchanges and that the regulated P2P regime launched in March 2024.
limitations: AFSA disclosed the month but not the exact launch day in the FAQ excerpt reviewed.

claims.statement: AFSA's public FAQ says Kazakhstan residents may trade on AFSA-licensed exchanges, retail clients have a USD 1,000 monthly fiat funding limit under AIFC bank-interaction rules, and Kazakhstan-resident legal entities can be clients only if they are miners, mining pools, or Professional Clients.
limitations: The reviewed source is an AFSA FAQ rather than a full legal codification package.

claims.statement: Official Binance surfaces indicate Binance Pay launched for Kazakhstan in 2025 and later integrated crypto payments with AlatauCityBank QR codes.
limitations: Both current public proofs were retained via official search snippets because direct pages no longer rendered normally.

claims.statement: Kazakhstan-facing Binance materials publicly surface Spot, Margin, Convert, Earn, Loans, Launchpool, OTC and trading-bot related product paths, but product-specific eligibility can still depend on account, jurisdiction, campaign or asset restrictions.
limitations: Public surface visibility is not identical to universal resident eligibility.

claims.statement: Binance Futures, futures account onboarding, and options references are publicly visible on Kazakhstan-facing surfaces.
limitations: This claim covers public surface visibility, not an unqualified statement that every resident is eligible for every derivatives product.

claims.statement: A Kazakhstan-specific official announcement snippet states Binance Kazakhstan expanded product availability in March 2025 to include options, futures copy trading and derivatives for all users.
limitations: The supporting announcement currently survives only as an official search snippet.

claims.statement: Binance's global Travel Rule page lists Kazakhstan among implemented Travel Rule jurisdictions.
Simple Earn is publicly available as a platform surface; Binance states the product can involve on-chain staking through staking pools, validators and nodes.
limitations: Some Earn/staking products can vary by asset and region.

claims.statement: Copy Trading is publicly surfaced on Kazakhstan-facing Binance pages, and Binance publishes an official Futures Copy Trading guide.
limitations: Copy Trading settings, minimums and eligible symbols can change.

claims.statement: Binance Launchpool is publicly visible and Binance states that only users who completed identity verification and reside in an eligible jurisdiction may participate.
limitations: The condition means Kazakhstan participation cannot be inferred solely from page visibility.

claims.statement: Binance Launchpad exists as a global Binance token-launch platform, but current Kazakhstan-specific Launchpad eligibility is not fully confirmed by direct current public terms; the strongest Kazakhstan-specific evidence found is a historical Kazakhstan-localized Launchpad announcement snippet.
limitations: Kazakhstan-specific evidence for Launchpad currently depends partly on a historical/localized announcement rather than a fully rendered current eligibility page.

claims.statement: Binance announced in June 2026 that the current NFT service on Binance Exchange would cease support on 2026-07-03 and users needed to withdraw transferable NFTs to Binance Wallet or a compatible wallet.
limitations: Current evidence is retained via official search snippet because the direct announcement page redirected during checking.

claims.statement: At least one official Binance Gift Card FAQ lists Kazakhstan among redemption-restricted jurisdictions, so Gift Card availability should not be assumed for Kazakhstan.
Binance Card exists as a global product currently available only in selected countries/jurisdictions, and the reviewed public materials do not explicitly confirm Kazakhstan as currently eligible.
limitations: A regional fee table references 'some CIS region', but the reviewed public card materials do not explicitly name Kazakhstan.

claims.statement: Binance publishes institutional/corporate services globally, and Binance Link was publicly launched in Kazakhstan in April 2025 for B2B2C enterprises using the licensed Kazakhstan entity.

The public referral offer page advertises fee-rebate rewards up to USD 1,000 for the referrer and up to USD 1,100 for the friend after sign-up, a USD 50+ crypto purchase and USD 100+ Spot or Convert trading.

The reviewed public referral notes disqualify certain jurisdictions such as Israel, Japan-linked flows, Nigeria and the UK from parts of the referral program, but do not affirmatively confirm Kazakhstan's current eligibility for the visible public offer.
limitations: Absence of a Kazakhstan ban in the reviewed note set is not the same as affirmative Kazakhstan eligibility.

claims.statement: Binance also maintains an affiliate restricted-countries guide that forbids incentive/referral content targeted at listed restricted countries and at any country on Binance's prohibited-country list.

No owner-approved CryptoBonusWorld Binance campaign URL or referral code was supplied in Issue #84, so a CBW-specific Binance offer cannot be verified beyond public Binance offer visibility and public terms review.
Binance publishes support and complaint routes including a support center with 24/7 chat access, formal complaint procedure, P2P appeal process, and a law-enforcement request portal.

Binance's public fee materials show a standard spot baseline of 0.1% maker / 0.1% taker for regular users, a BNB trading-fee discount option, a public futures fee schedule, and network-specific crypto withdrawal fees.
limitations: Live asset-specific withdrawal fees and event discounts can change at any time.

claims.statement: Binance P2P is publicly documented as an escrow-style marketplace and platform fee schedules can vary by market role or merchant status.
Kazakhstan public-history sources show Binance cooperation with Kazakhstan on compliance and education initiatives, including the 2022 FMA MoU and 2023 university/teacher training support.
An official Binance search snippet states Binance Wallet's full suite of features rolled out in Kazakhstan on 2025-11-04.
limitations: The current archived page did not fully render; support is based on an official search snippet.
